item.title: Weathering-derived calcium supports carbon storage in grassland soils
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 13 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04142-2

Mineral weathering-derived calcium promotes soil organic carbon storage in US Mollisols, and agriculture has increased calcium inputs four- to fivefold, altering the geochemical conditions that sustain carbon in these soils, based on continental-scale datasets and geochemical modelling.
item.dc:title: Weathering-derived calcium supports carbon storage in grassland soils

item.title: Physics-informed deep learning links geodetic data and fault friction
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 12 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04138-y

Spatially variable frictional properties along a fault can be estimated using a physics-informed neural network approach that enables physics-consistent slip modelling, as tested on the 2010 Bungo slow slip event in southwest Japan.
item.dc:title: Physics-informed deep learning links geodetic data and fault friction

item.title: Baltic Sea sediment bacterial communities show asymmetric and incomplete recovery after reciprocal temperature change translocation
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 12 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04147-x

Ocean warming will alter bacterial communities of Baltic Sea coastal sediments and associated biogeochemical cycles, according to translocation experiments of Baltic Sea sediment.
item.dc:title: Baltic Sea sediment bacterial communities show asymmetric and incomplete recovery after reciprocal temperature change translocation

item.title: Social vulnerability amplifies global inequality in urban heat risk
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 11 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04137-z

Urban heat risk increased worldwide during 2000–2019, with growth in the Global South nearly five times that in the Global North, and conventional approaches underestimate North-South inequality by nearly 65 percent, according to an analysis of 1,029 global cities.
item.dc:title: Social vulnerability amplifies global inequality in urban heat risk

item.title: Episodic isolation of the Arctic Mediterranean from the North Atlantic during late Pleistocene glacials
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 11 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04133-3

Highly dynamic coupling between the Arctic Mediterranean and the North Atlantic during late Pleistocene glaciations; as shown using Beryllium isotopes from sediment cores from the Arctic Ocean, the Nordic Seas and the North Atlantic.
item.dc:title: Episodic isolation of the Arctic Mediterranean from the North Atlantic during late Pleistocene glacials

item.title: Impact of climate change on the photovoltaic power potential in Sweden across 21st century
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 11 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04091-w

Future climate change is projected to increase solar photovoltaic power generation in Sweden by about 5% compared to historical periods, while optimized panel tilt can boost output by 3 to 6%; according to a validated installation model incorporating air temperature, solar radiation, and snow conditions across four cities under future climate scenarios.
item.dc:title: Impact of climate change on the photovoltaic power potential in Sweden across 21st century
